pros: Intuitive interpretation of local network density
Useful for detecting communities and cliques
Normalized between 0 and 1 for easy comparison
Robust indicator of small-world network properties
Simple to compute for individual nodes
Reveals functional modules in biological networks
Differentiates random networks from real-world networks
cons: Computationally expensive for large dense graphs O(V³)
Local measure only captures immediate neighborhood
Sensitive to nodes with low degree (degree < 2 returns 0)
Average local clustering biased by low-degree nodes
Global and average local measures can give different results
Does not capture higher-order clustering (squares, etc.)
Limited to undirected graphs without adaptation
